whoIsThisFor.heading: Who should take the B2B Commerce Administrator AP exam?

personas.label: Salesforce admins managing B2B storefronts
personas.description: You manage a B2B Commerce store and want to show that you can set it up and run it.

personas.label: Implementation partners
personas.description: You build B2B stores for clients and want to show that you understand the setup from start to finish.

personas.label: Operations leads
personas.description: You manage online ordering for business buyers and want to understand products, pricing, and buyer access.

examDifficulty.heading: Is the B2B Commerce Administrator AP exam hard?
examDifficulty.summary: The exam covers practical admin tasks, but the passing score is high. Learn the setup steps well so you can apply them to real situations.
bullets: 60 scored questions in 90 minutes, plus up to five unscored questions that do not count.
75% to pass, which is 45 correct answers out of 60.
Setup order matters: Know what must be configured before a buyer can see products or check out.
Hands-on practice helps: Build a test store to make the setup steps familiar.
examDifficulty.passRateGuidance: Build a store in a trial or sandbox org before the exam. Aim for at least 85% on practice tests before booking, since the passing score is high.

examFormat.heading: B2B Commerce Administrator AP exam format
examFormat.intro: Accredited Professional exams are taken online. Here is what to expect:
examFormat.scenarioPercent: Many questions describe an admin problem, such as a buyer who cannot see a product or a price that looks wrong. Choose what to set up or fix.
bestWayToPass: Follow the buyer-to-product setup: Buyer account, buyer group, entitlement policy, catalog, and price book must work together.
Know when to rebuild the search index: Changes to products and categories may not appear until the index is rebuilt.
Learn checkout: Know where pricing, tax, shipping, inventory, and payment checks happen.
Practice in a store: Create a buyer, grant access, and place a test order.

certificationCard.description: This exam tests how to set up and run a Salesforce B2B Commerce store, including buyers, products, catalogs, pricing, search, and checkout. The exam is 60 scored questions in 90 minutes, with a 75% pass mark, weighted towards Salesforce B2B Commerce App and Storefront Deployment (20% each).

keyConcepts.h2: B2B Commerce Admin AP: Key Concepts for the Exam

blocks.heading: Store Setup & Storefront Configuration
blocks.body: A B2B store is created in the Commerce app and runs on an Experience Cloud site. Use Experience Builder to design the site. Store settings include currency, language, buyer access, and checkout. Link the store to its catalogs and buyer groups. You can let guests browse products before logging in, but a buyer account is still needed to place an order. Test changes in a sandbox or test store first.

blocks.heading: Product Catalog & Pricing
blocks.body: Products are organized in a **catalog** and **categories**. A product can be simple or have variations, such as size and color. Set up a variation parent and variation attributes so buyers can select an option. Prices come from **price books** assigned to buyer groups. If a buyer cannot see a price, check the price book linked to their group. After you change products, categories, or searchable fields, **rebuild the search index** so the store shows the changes.

blocks.heading: Buyer Account & Contact Management
blocks.body: A business customer is an Account enabled as a **buyer account**. Its Contacts can be set up as **buyer users**, who are external users that sign in to the store. Add buyer accounts to **buyer groups**. Groups link to **entitlement policies**, which control which products buyers can see and buy, and to price books, which set prices. To change access for many customers, update the buyer group rather than each account.

blocks.heading: Order Management & Checkout
blocks.body: Checkout takes a buyer from cart to order. It can check inventory, calculate price, shipping, and tax, and take payment. These steps may connect to outside systems. After an order is placed, it is stored as an Order in Salesforce. With Salesforce Order Management, an **Order Summary** tracks fulfillment, changes, and returns. Buyers can reorder from their order history. Admins can also set approval steps or purchase limits.

blocks.heading: Integration with Salesforce CRM
blocks.body: The store runs in Salesforce, so sales and service teams can use the same Accounts, Contacts, Orders, and Cases. Reps can see what customers ordered online, and service agents can handle order questions in Cases. Reports and dashboards can include online orders. An ERP system may provide prices, stock levels, and order status through an integration.

scenarioTips.h2: How to pass the B2B Commerce Administrator AP exam
scenarioTips.intro: Many questions ask why a buyer cannot see or buy something, or how to set up a change for many buyers. Follow the steps from the buyer to the product.

blocks.heading: Store Setup & Configuration
blocks.body: A store runs on an Experience Cloud site. Currency, language, and guest browsing are set for each store.

blocks.heading: Product Catalog Management
blocks.body: Products go in catalogs and categories. Rebuild the search index after changes so buyers see updated information.

blocks.heading: Buyer Groups & Entitlements
blocks.body: If a buyer cannot see a product, check the entitlement policy on their buyer group. If they cannot see a price, check the group’s price book.

blocks.heading: Cart & Checkout Configuration
blocks.body: Checkout may check inventory, price, shipping, tax, and payment. Each step may connect to another system.

blocks.heading: Order Management Integration
blocks.body: Placed orders become Salesforce Orders. With Order Management, Order Summaries track fulfillment and returns.

nextCertsAfter.heading: Next Certifications After This AP
nextCertsAfter.intro: Good next steps after B2B Commerce Admin:

sampleQuestions.question: A buyer signs in but cannot see a new product line. The products are in the catalog. What should the admin check first?
options: Check the entitlement policy for the buyer group
Check the buyer’s password
Check the store’s color theme
Check the length of the product description field
sampleQuestions.explanation: Entitlement policies control which products a buyer group can see. Add the product to the right policy.
whyWrong: A wrong password would stop the buyer from signing in.
The store theme changes its appearance, not product access.
Description length does not control product visibility.

sampleQuestions.question: A buyer can see a product but no price appears. What is the most likely cause?
options: The search index was rebuilt recently, so prices have not been refreshed yet
The product is not in a price book assigned to the buyer group
The product has no image
The cart has too many items
sampleQuestions.explanation: The buyer group needs a price book with a price for that product. Without a matching entry, the buyer will not see a price.
whyWrong: A recent index rebuild does not remove a product price.
An image is not needed to show the price.
Cart size does not control product prices.

sampleQuestions.question: An admin renamed categories and added products, but buyers still see the old names. What should the admin do?
options: Change buyer profiles
Delete and recreate the store
Rebuild the search index
Ask buyers to clear their browser cache
sampleQuestions.explanation: The store uses a search index for product search and navigation. Rebuild it so buyers can see product and category changes.
whyWrong: Profiles do not control product or category names.
Recreating the store is unnecessary and could remove its setup.
The old names are in the search index, not the buyers’ browser cache.

sampleQuestions.question: A company wants 300 customer accounts to receive a new 10% price list. What is the most efficient method?
options: Edit the price setup for each of the 300 accounts, one account at a time
Create a new store for each account
Ask buyers to enter a discount code
Assign the price book to the buyer group for those accounts
sampleQuestions.explanation: Assign the new price book to the buyer group so the change applies to all its accounts.
whyWrong: Changing 300 accounts one by one takes longer and can lead to errors.
One store can serve many buyer accounts.
A discount code depends on each buyer entering it.

sampleQuestions.question: What must happen before a contact at a customer company can sign in and place orders?
options: Enable the account as a buyer account and create a buyer user for the contact
The contact needs a Sales Cloud license and a role above the account owner in the hierarchy
The contact must be a Salesforce admin
Mark the account as a competitor
sampleQuestions.explanation: Enable the Account as a buyer account, then set up its Contact as an external buyer user.
whyWrong: External buyers do not need an internal Sales Cloud license.
Buyers are external users, not Salesforce admins.
Competitor status does not control store access.

sampleQuestions.question: Visitors should browse products before signing in, but only signed-in buyers can order. What should be enabled?
options: A second store for guests
Guest browsing for the store
Self-registration
Public Read/Write access on all objects
sampleQuestions.explanation: Guest browsing lets visitors view the catalog without signing in. Checkout still requires a buyer account.
whyWrong: A second store is not needed for guest browsing.
Self-registration does not by itself let people browse before signing in.
Opening all objects would create a serious security risk.

sampleQuestions.question: A T-shirt comes in three sizes and four colors. How should it appear in the catalog?
options: Twelve separate products
A separate category for each color
One variation parent with size and color attributes
One product with all the sizes and colors in its description
sampleQuestions.explanation: Set up a variation parent with size and color attributes so buyers can choose an option on one product page.
whyWrong: Twelve separate products make browsing harder and repeat the product setup.
Categories organize products; they do not create selectable size and color options.
A description cannot let buyers select or price a product variation.

sampleQuestions.question: Which record links buyer accounts to the products they can see and the prices they pay?
options: The store theme
The search index
The checkout flow
The buyer group
sampleQuestions.explanation: Buyer groups link accounts to entitlement policies and price books.
whyWrong: The theme controls how the store looks.
The search index helps find products; it does not control access.
Checkout handles the order, not product access or pricing.

sampleQuestions.question: During checkout, the store must check stock in the company’s ERP. Where should this happen?
options: In the checkout inventory step through an ERP integration
In the buyer’s profile
In a weekly report
In the product description, updated by hand whenever stock changes
sampleQuestions.explanation: The checkout inventory step can use an integration to check current stock in the ERP.
whyWrong: Profiles control user details and access, not stock levels.
A weekly report is too late for a checkout stock check.
A product description cannot check inventory.

sampleQuestions.question: A sales rep wants to see what a customer ordered in the B2B store. Where can they look?
options: Ask the customer
On the customer’s Salesforce Account
In the store theme settings
Only in a separate commerce system
sampleQuestions.explanation: B2B Commerce runs in Salesforce, and orders are linked to the customer’s Account.
whyWrong: Sales reps can check the order in Salesforce.
The store theme does not store order data.
B2B Commerce is part of Salesforce, not a separate system.

sampleQuestions.question: After an order is placed, the team needs to track fulfillment, changes, and returns. What should it use?
options: Chatter posts
A spreadsheet
Salesforce Order Management and Order Summaries
The cart record, kept open after checkout for each order
sampleQuestions.explanation: Order Management creates an Order Summary to track an order through fulfillment, changes, and returns.
whyWrong: Chatter is for collaboration, not order tracking.
A spreadsheet is manual and separate from Salesforce.
The cart is used before the order is placed.

sampleQuestions.question: The store must sell in US dollars and euros. Where should this be set?
options: In each product name, with the currency code added as a suffix by hand
In the buyers’ passwords
In the search index
In store currency settings, with price books for each currency
sampleQuestions.explanation: Set the currencies in the store and use price books with prices for each currency.
whyWrong: Product names do not set currency.
Passwords do not affect prices or currency.
The search index does not set currency.

sampleQuestions.question: An admin wants to change the store home page without code. Which tool should they use?
options: Experience Builder
Workbench
Developer Console
Data Loader
sampleQuestions.explanation: B2B stores use Experience Cloud sites. Experience Builder lets admins change pages with drag-and-drop tools.
whyWrong: Workbench is for queries and API tasks.
Developer Console is used for code.
Data Loader moves data.

sampleQuestions.question: A product should only be sold to buyers in the Healthcare group. How should the admin set this up?
options: Remove the product from all price books
Add the product to the Healthcare group’s entitlement policy
Put “Healthcare only” in the product name and rely on buyers to notice it
Hide the product with CSS
sampleQuestions.explanation: Entitlement policies control which buyer groups can see and buy a product.
whyWrong: Removing it from all price books also stops Healthcare buyers from purchasing it.
Text in a product name does not prevent other groups from seeing it. CSS only hides a product; it does not control access.

sampleQuestions.question: Buyers often order the same items each month. Which feature saves them time?
options: Download the catalog as a PDF
Call customer service each month
Reorder from their order history
Create a new account for each order
sampleQuestions.explanation: Buyers can reorder from past orders, which puts the same items in the cart in one step.
whyWrong: A PDF catalog does not place an order.
Calling customer service takes longer.
Creating new accounts adds work and loses order history.
